extra.message: Attacker-controlled request.path is interpolated into template source passed to render_template_string(). A crafted nonexistent URL can execute arbitrary Jinja expressions and potentially achieve server-side code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The Flask signing key is hardcoded in source. Anyone knowing it can create valid Flask session cookies, including forged Flask-Login user identifiers, and impersonate users or administrators.
A fixed registration credential is inserted into every fresh database. Anyone with source access can use this known value to bypass the invitation gate and create an account.
The startup seed creates predictable user and administrator accounts with plaintext source-known passwords user and admin. Remote attackers can authenticate directly as the seeded administrator.
SQLAlchemy echo logging is enabled unconditionally. SQL statements and bound parameters, including emails, password hashes, note contents, and registration codes, are written to application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The search query parameter is interpolated directly into a SQLAlchemy text() fragment. Attackers can alter the WHERE clause and read notes belonging to other users, including private notes.
The user-supplied registration code is interpolated directly into SQL passed to session.execute(). This permits attacker-controlled SQL syntax in the registration-code lookup.
An unsigned, attacker-controlled cookie is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads() before every request. A malicious pickle can execute arbitrary code without authentication.

A profile-image URL supplied through request form data is passed directly to urlopen() without scheme, hostname, address, or redirect validation. Attackers can access internal services and use supported schemes such as file:// to read local files.
The server fetches an attacker-selected resource without a timeout and reads the entire response without a size limit. Slow or extremely large responses can occupy workers or exhaust server memory.

Account form fields are copied directly into current_user.__dict__. Because AccountForm exposes is_admin and the filter does not exclude it, any authenticated user can submit is_admin=true and grant themselves administrator privileges.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The user_id path parameter is used to retrieve all notes without verifying it equals current_user.id. Any authenticated user can enumerate account IDs and read another user's private notes.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: A note is loaded solely by attacker-controlled note_id and deleted without checking note.user_id against the authenticated user. Any logged-in user can delete any other user's note.

extra.message: User-controlled note text is stored without sanitization and rendered with Jinja's safe filter. An attacker can create a public note containing script-capable HTML that executes for other authenticated users.

extra.message: Password changes do not require the existing password. The server only compares two attacker-controlled form values before replacing the stored password hash, enabling account takeover through a captured session or forged request.

Changing a password only updates the database record; existing Flask-Login sessions are not revoked or version-checked. Previously stolen session cookies remain authenticated after the password change.
The login handler performs unlimited password checks without throttling, lockout, or request-rate enforcement. Remote attackers can repeatedly guess passwords for known accounts.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: bcrypt checkpw() is only executed when an email exists. The substantial timing difference between unknown and registered emails provides a remote account-enumeration oracle.

The login endpoint accepts a cross-site POST without a CSRF token. An attacker can force a victim's browser to authenticate as an attacker-controlled account, causing later victim data to be stored in that account.
Logout is implemented as a state-changing GET request without CSRF protection. A third-party page can cause an authenticated browser to request this URL and terminate the user's session.

The note-creation endpoint uses a raw WTForms Form and performs no CSRF validation. A forged request can create attacker-selected note content in a victim's account, including persistent XSS payloads.
The note-deletion POST endpoint has no CSRF-token validation. An attacker can submit a cross-site request that deletes a note using the victim's authenticated session.
The profile-image update uses a raw WTForms Form without CSRF validation. A forged request can force an authenticated victim to trigger the server-side URL fetch against an attacker-selected target.

The account-update endpoint has no CSRF protection. A forged POST can change a victim's email and password and set is_admin=true through the mass-assignment sink, enabling account takeover and privilege escalation.

The administrator registration-code endpoint performs a state-changing POST without validating a CSRF token. A cross-site request can cause an authenticated administrator to generate unauthorized registration credentials.

The supplied deployment configuration exposes only plaintext HTTP listeners and defines no TLS listener or redirect. Login passwords and authenticated session cookies can be transmitted over the network without encryption.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The home-page query loads every matching Note and joined User object with all() and has no pagination or result limit. Authenticated users can create unbounded public notes, causing excessive database work, memory consumption, and response generation for every user.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
